data.review_body:
I'm so disappointed with AliExpress!!! I had previously had good experiences as a buyer, but now I'm facing an outrageous situation, and I can't find any way to contact AliExpress customer support. My order number is: 5551106010096930
I received 10 m² of wallpaper with the image distorted and different from the product description. I opened Dispute #27679052 on June 25, 2026. Following the dispute instructions, I returned the items on July 3, 2026, paying $30 for return shipping. I attached the tracking number (CB800393193MD) to the dispute and also sent it to the seller together with the tracking webpage. I did everything required so that I could receive my $100 refund.
Immediately after I opened the dispute, the seller, "Simple-fashion," stopped responding to all of my messages. My return package has been in China since July 14, and its current tracking status is "Invoice missing." It appears that the seller has not provided the required information about the parcel's value or confirmed that it is a returned package.
According to the dispute, I will receive my refund only after the seller receives the returned package. However, it seems that the seller is deliberately ignoring both my messages and the return shipment. My dispute is scheduled to expire on August 2, and I'm afraid I will lose my refund even though I have fully complied with all the requirements.
I have every possible piece of evidence showing that I followed the return process correctly and that the seller is ignoring the return. However, I cannot reach a human customer support representative. I can only communicate with an automated chatbot. There is no customer support email address, no clear information about customer service hours, and, most importantly, no clear way to contact a real person for assistance.

Can someone from AliExpress please review my case and help resolve this issue before my dispute expires?!!!

data.review_body:
AliExpress customer support? Absolutely world-class. You open a dispute and they hit you with a copy-paste "sorry we can't help, best of luck out there" faster than the package took to arrive. But the second my bank got involved for a chargeback? Suddenly these guys are VERY responsive
fired off a neat little email to my bank claiming they'd tried to resolve everything. Then my bank asked for actual evidence of that. Crickets
And here's the cherry on top - they request evidence from customers via an email address that doesn't receive emails. Let that sink in. They set up a dead-end email, wave it around as proof they're "communicating," then vanish the moment anyone asks for receipts. In most countries we have a word for that. CRIME
Stellar operation you're running, guys.
data.review_headline: AliExpress dispute process or a masterclass in doing nothing
